page_note: Page 144 spans a layer boundary. Segments 0-11 close Kephalaion 56 with pastoral exhortation ('my brothers, my beloveds, my members') — pure hortatory layer. Segments 12-13 are the editorial chapter apparatus (number + title). Segments 14-15 are the apostolic dialogue frame with a strong seam flag (Babylonian catechumen asking the Illuminator). From segment 16 onward, however, the disciple's question becomes substantively cosmological-anthropogonic — concerning Adam the first man, the manner of his molding/begetting, his stature, his strength, and the difference between his generation and present human begetting. This is the Persian/substratic question structure beneath the Kephalaia: a substantive cosmogonic question that the editorial frame merely wraps. The strong negative editorial fatigue score (-3.59) reflects the page transitioning OUT OF the hortatory tail of Keph 56 INTO the substrate question of Keph 57. Damage in the second half (lacunae {2}-{7}) affects the Adam-begetting question.
